title: Check the story
pitch: About 3 minutes. It pulls apart what happened from the story you told yourself, because the story is usually the part that hurts, and it's rarely the only one that fits.

cards.prompt: About 3 minutes. It pulls apart what happened from the story you told yourself, because the story is usually the part that hurts, and it's rarely the only one that fits.
How do you feel right now?
cards.why: A number now lets you see at the end whether anything eased.

cards.prompt: What happened? Just the facts, like a camera would see it.
cards.why: Writing just the facts gives you solid ground before any meaning gets added.

cards.prompt: What did you tell yourself it meant?
cards.why: Once the story is in words, it's something you can question instead of only feel.
options: This is going to end badly

cards.prompt: What fits that story, and what doesn't?
cards.why: Weighing both sides lets the facts decide how true it is, not the feeling.
options: Nothing really, it's just a feeling
They did seem off, but not at me
Some of it fits, some doesn't

cards.prompt: If a friend told you this, what else might it mean?
cards.why: A second reading gives you a choice in how you respond.
options: They might be tired or stressed
It might be about their day, not me
I might be missing part of the picture
It was one bad moment, not the whole story
I don't know yet, and I can ask

cards.prompt: How do you feel right now?
cards.why: Comparing with the start shows you what these few minutes did.
